reuse.why: Puts the daily rule into the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend (via a new frequency argument) and updates all three of its callers, but the template adds its own resolveSkippedWeekend wrapper instead of a shared one.

duplication.why: Each caller still carries its own `skipWeekend ? getDateWithSkippedWeekend(...) : date` dispatch plus its own way of dropping null occurrences (a for-loop in getNextDate, filter/slice in getUpcomingDates, a nullable loop in schedule-template), and resolveSkippedWeekend is a third copy of that dispatch.

placement.why: The frequency rule sits in shared/schedules.ts with the weekend helper, but the enable-flag-plus-null wrapper lives privately in budget/schedule-template.ts rather than next to it.

scope.why: Changes track the request, with some incidental renaming (date to occurrence, dates to occurrences) and a release note.

maintainability.why: A nullable result from the shared helper forces every caller to re-implement over-fetching and skipping, with a magic lookahead constant and a template loop whose termination now depends on two nullable variables.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All callers still use getDateWithSkippedWeekend for the weekend decision.

disguised_duplication.where: resolveSkippedWeekend in budget/schedule-template.ts repackages the same skipWeekend-gated call that getNextDate (shared/schedules.ts) and getUpcomingDates (server/schedules/app.ts) inline, and the null-skipping iteration is reshaped differently at each of the three sites.

one_place.where: The daily-skip rule itself is the `frequency === 'daily'` branch in getDateWithSkippedWeekend (shared/schedules.ts), used by getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and the budget schedule template; only the enable dispatch and null handling are repeated per caller.
